Lemma 6.28 (Product Fourier–Wiener calculus). For scalar f ∈ AI , convolution by f on L2 (GI ) is
trace class and
                                ∥Kf ∥S1 (L2 (GI )) = ∥f ∥AI .                               (63)
If I ⊂ I ′ , lifting f by independence of the coordinates in I ′ \ I preserves the norm. Pointwise multiplication
satisfies
                                              ∥f g∥AI ≤ ∥f ∥AI ∥g∥AI .                                       (64)
The same inequalities hold coefficientwise in the declared finite projective marked norm. Left/right
translations, inversion, and coordinate permutations are isometries.
Proof. Peter–Weyl decomposes L2 (GI ) into the blocks Vλ ⊗ Vλ∗ . Convolution has block fb(λ) ⊗ I, whose
trace norm is dλ ∥fb(λ)∥S1 ; summing gives (63). A lifted function has only the trivial Fourier block in
every added coordinate, proving isometry. The standard coefficient-product formula, complete contraction
in the unitary Clebsch–Gordan maps, and the projective trace norm give (64). The remaining symmetries
are unitary changes of Peter–Weyl blocks.

Lemma 6.32 (Cutoff-uniform junction row). Every fixed bulk, toron, seam, reflection, or wrapping
junction has operator norm at most one constant J∗ < ∞, independent of the Peter–Weyl cutoff. At
every fixed passive mark order k ≤ 3 + Q, the corresponding coefficientwise constants J∗,k are finite and
cutoff independent.
Proof. In block-first Hilbert normalization, Clebsch–Gordan recouplings are unitary, invariant-channel
maps are orthogonal projections, and translations and inversion are unitary. All remaining maps belong
to a finite bounded-incidence template set. Passive marks differentiate only the fixed local coefficient
maps and are controlled by the fixed-Q marked row.

                                                                   −1
Proof. On an oriented path, write the pivot increment as Xp = Yp,−    Yp,+ . The triangular change from
pivot increments to successive cumulative products has unit Haar Jacobian. The one-pivot density
                                             −1
therefore gives the convolution kernel ρp (Yp,− Yp,+ ). Every multipivot activity depends on the same
increments and hence multiplies the product-group convolution density hU,F itself; it is not used as a
Schur multiplier on an already-formed trace-class kernel. Reversed orientations are handled by inversion,
which is isometric in A.

   Lemma 6.28 identifies the trace norm of convolution on L2 (GU ) with the Fourier–Wiener norm and
supplies the Banach-algebra and lifting properties. Together with the Lemma 6.29 and the definition of
wA,k give the unmarked estimate. At order k, Leibniz marks at most k one-pivot densities or activities;
replacing those unmarked norms by their marked norms produces CQ,k , not an exponential-in-|U | loss. This
gives (86). This is the step that treats same-edge and cross-edge activities in one actual tensor-product
cut space.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

E     Invariant tensor spaces through engineering dimension six
The low-dimensional color input can be stated without choosing a basis. The degree-two invariant
polynomial is unique for every simple g. A primitive degree-three invariant occurs only for Ar , r ≥ 2.
Hence the reflection-even dimension-four scalar block is one-dimensional for every G, while the dimension-
six block may contain the additional cubic curvature contraction in type A. The antisymmetric structure

and epsilon contractions, invariant color tensors, total-difference classes, and equation-of-motion contacts
through the declared engineering cutoff. No argument relies on a hand-picked SU(2) basis once this
quotient is used.

6.5    Exact Haar–optical matching law

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the

whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.

   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial

tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.
After removal of already reported physical cross-core connectors, such a history factorizes into one-core
expectations or empty-support scalars and is assigned by the exact owner map to the normalized one-core
references or the pre-existing regular/Gaussian inventory.
   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial
internal flux, has a deterministic visited-set exploration. Order incident half-edges before marking an
unoriented edge inspected. Discovery edges form a rooted spanning tree; each merger, reconnection, shared
tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family

    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.

is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).

gives (86). This is the step that treats same-edge and cross-edge activities in one actual tensor-product
cut space.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

Theorem 6.39 (Exact incidence-split product-group nuclear compact collect). Choose R and a finite
pivot count N from the unmarked conditions (84), (95), and (96), with N ≥ 3. These choices are made
once and are independent of source order. Then, for every fixed Q < ∞, after exact compact integration
the complete nonvacuum compact coefficients satisfy (99), uniformly through three passive optical marks
and Q physical-source marks. The constants have the Cauchy growth of one common positive source
radius.
Proof. Expand the exact single-denominator amplitude once by Lemma 6.34 and split every activity
by (71). For each family, absorb all covered-pivot densities and all same-edge or cross-edge activity
factors into the one product-group convolution operator of Lemma 6.35. Its Fourier–Wiener norm pays
the actual tensor-product nuclear cost. The scalar incidence reserve pays that cost and every lost Haar
contraction, while the promoted activity magnitude remains once for the canonical rooted exploration.
Clean activity-free physical cycles are closed at the deterministic pivots in Rg (F). The strict unmarked
recursion fixes R and N once. At every finite marked order the same-order coefficient is still qsp < 1
and all new terms are lower-triangular forcing, so source order changes constants but not the chosen
geometry. The marked triangular extension sums all carrier branches, physical cycles, shared tails, seams,
reflections, wrapping edges, and activity hyperedges. The resulting majorant proves absolute convergence
of the family expansion and permits the cutoff and finite-subfamily limits. The final spatial allocation
gives (99).

6.5.1 Compact collect with optical field live
The matching theorem is now proved on one exact joint law, before the normal/optical variables are
marginalized. This is the decisive ordering. The compact retained variables are reduced conditionally by
Haar–pivot integration; the resulting activities remain functions of the complete optical field; and only
then is the connected logarithm taken by the marked Gaussian forest theorem. Thus no retained density,
latent mixture, or residual-only gas is inserted between the physical law and the connected source kernel.

Lemma 6.32 (Cutoff-uniform junction row). Every fixed bulk, toron, seam, reflection, or wrapping
junction has operator norm at most one constant J∗ < ∞, independent of the Peter–Weyl cutoff. At
every fixed passive mark order k ≤ 3 + Q, the corresponding coefficientwise constants J∗,k are finite and
cutoff independent.
Proof. In block-first Hilbert normalization, Clebsch–Gordan recouplings are unitary, invariant-channel
maps are orthogonal projections, and translations and inversion are unitary. All remaining maps belong
to a finite bounded-incidence template set. Passive marks differentiate only the fixed local coefficient
maps and are controlled by the fixed-Q marked row.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

6.5.1 Compact collect with optical field live
The matching theorem is now proved on one exact joint law, before the normal/optical variables are
marginalized. This is the decisive ordering. The compact retained variables are reduced conditionally by
Haar–pivot integration; the resulting activities remain functions of the complete optical field; and only
then is the connected logarithm taken by the marked Gaussian forest theorem. Thus no retained density,
latent mixture, or residual-only gas is inserted between the physical law and the connected source kernel.

Lemma 6.23 (Tri-graded optical/source upgrade). In the exact factorization of Theorem 6.10, the

   The maps V 7→ e−V − 1, multiplication, inversion of the strictly positive scalar denominator, and

Leibniz, Faà di Bruno, and the quotient rule are paid by the three factorial weights in (56). Since G
is fixed, the derivative orders 2sG , three, and two are fixed finite integers, so the resulting constant is
uniform in all declared limits. This proves the stated tri-graded row without identifying an optical field
derivative with a passive source derivative.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.
After removal of already reported physical cross-core connectors, such a history factorizes into one-core
expectations or empty-support scalars and is assigned by the exact owner map to the normalized one-core
references or the pre-existing regular/Gaussian inventory.
   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial
internal flux, has a deterministic visited-set exploration. Order incident half-edges before marking an
unoriented edge inspected. Discovery edges form a rooted spanning tree; each merger, reconnection, shared
tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

 Yang–Mills Existence, Mass Gap, and Nontriviality
for Fixed Compact Simple Gauge Groups via Karcher
      Blocking and Exact Haar–Pivot Matching
                                             Harold D. Kirk III1,2,∗
                         1
                             University of Memphis, Memphis, Tennessee 38152, USA
                                        2
                                            ORCID: 0009-0000-6014-8451

                                                August 3, 2026


                                                     Abstract
        Let G be a fixed compact connected simple Lie group and let ρ be a fixed faithful finite-dimensional
    unitary representation. We construct four-dimensional pure G Yang–Mills theory as a zero-spacing,
    infinite-volume limit of reflection-positive Wilson lattice measures. The Wilson plaquette function
    is normalized at the identity to the background quadratic form used to define the coupling u = g 2 .
    A weighted forty-nine-path Karcher block, complete sixteen-alias normal section, charged chart-
    complement partition, and permanent rooted domain produce a uniform scale-two map on a centered
    invariant graph,
                                                 11 CA (G) log 2
                               u(2L) = u(L) +                    u(L)2 + OG (u(L)3 ).
                                                     24π 2

    The complete linear block certificate is independent of color and tensors with Ig ; all nonlinear
    constants are finite and may depend on G. At the physical handoff, a group-dependent product
    Sobolev order 2sG > dG /2 gives a Peter–Weyl Fourier–Wiener landing for the exact one-pivot and
    multipivot densities. Separated Haar pivots contract nonvacuum compact flux, optical covariance
    contracts normal-field stretches, and all remaining vertices retain their support charge. A single
    marked replica–BKAR forest then gives a boundary-to-center two-root connector and one physical
    clustering rate. General invariant-jet transport, displacement and stress Ward identities, finite
    dimension-four mixing, and a dimension-six rotation regulator yield a tempered, reflection-positive,
    translation-continuous, O(4)-covariant Schwinger family. Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction gives a
    positive-energy Poincaré-covariant local theory with unique vacuum and a strictly positive Hamiltonian
    gap. Endpoint-safe curvature-source transport produces a nonzero local vector with positive spectral
    mass in a finite interval above the gap. The theorem concerns the local gauge-invariant curvature-jet
    observable theory. No estimate is asserted uniformly over the class of compact simple groups.

1     The compact-simple-group theorem and proof boundary
1.1    Problem and result
The constructive Yang–Mills problem asks for a nontrivial quantum gauge field theory on R4 satisfying
the Osterwalder–Schrader and Wightman requirements and possessing a strictly positive mass gap [1].
The physical scale, thermodynamic limit, zero lattice spacing, Euclidean covariance, local spectral content,
and non-abelian field geometry must be controlled in one compatible construction.
   Fix throughout a compact connected simple Lie group G, a faithful unitary representation ρ : G → U (Vρ )
of dimension dρ , and a positive normalization of the invariant quadratic form for which the adjoint color
factor is denoted CA (G). The Wilson plaquette function is
                                                        1
                                                                    
                                   wG,ρ (U ) = cρ 1 −     Re Tr ρ(U ) ,
                                                       dρ
where cρ > 0 is chosen once so that the Hessian at the identity is the quadratic form used by the
background-field coupling coordinate u = g 2 . This choice is a finite linear normalization of the bare
Wilson coupling and is part of the fixed-group input register.
Theorem 1.1 (Four-dimensional Yang–Mills construction for fixed compact simple G). For every fixed
pair (G, ρ) as above, there is a directed sequence of reflection-positive Wilson lattice measures, with
microscopic spacing tending to zero and periodic volume tending to infinity, whose local gauge-invariant
curvature-jet Schwinger functions converge to a nontrivial Euclidean field theory on R4 .
   The limiting Schwinger family is tempered, permutation symmetric, reflection positive, translation
continuous, exponentially clustering, and O(4) covariant. Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction yields a
positive-energy Poincaré-covariant local theory with a unique vacuum and a number m⋆ (G) > 0 such that
                                              H Ω⊥ ≥ m⋆ (G).

a nonzero reflected local curvature vector and positive spectral mass in a finite interval [m⋆ (G), M⋆ (G)].
1.2    Fixed-group conventions and finite register
Write g = Lie(G) and dG = dim G. All Haar measures are normalized. The finite-volume approximants
use the ordinary periodic link space GE(Λ) with periodic gauge transformations; no twisted boundary
condition or nontrivial finite-volume bundle sector is summed. This is sufficient for the claimed local
theory on the contractible space R4 . The bi-invariant metric, exponential coordinates, Laplacian ∆G ,
Casimir eigenvalues, and operator norms are those determined by the declared quadratic form. In
curvature formulas, Tr(XY ) denotes this normalized invariant bilinear pairing; raw representation traces
are written Tr ρ(·). Let                     

ordinary-periodic toron/seam template register, the adjoint color factor, and the finite invariant-jet
dimensions through the retained degree. Every statement called uniform is uniform in cutoff, volume,
directed depth, periodic wrapping, admitted exterior histories, and the finite reflected template family,

1.3     Proof architecture
The proof has four stages. First, the exact Karcher block is placed in a complete full-alias normal chart
and combined with a charged chart-complement partition, permanent analytic domain, marked connected
logarithm, Wick-stable jet block, and centered invariant graph. The folded spacetime symbol tensors
with Ig , while all nonlinear estimates are admitted by the finite register CG .
   Second, exact background-scheme conjugacy identifies the universal marginal coefficient      and a directed
schedule reaches the compact matching scale. The higher product Sobolev operator p (1 − ∆p )sG replaces
                                                                                       Q
the rank-one order and supplies the fixed-G Fourier–Wiener rows.
   Third, complete Haar and optical variables are kept in one partition function. A mixed replica–
BKAR forest makes every root-to-root path pay separated Haar contraction, optical covariance decay,
or pre-existing support charge. Ordinary-periodic toron backgrounds, seams, reflections, and wrapping
certificates enter only through the finite template theorem of Appendix D.
   Finally, a least-label source forest transports the complete invariant-jet system. The degree-four block
is group-independent because a compact simple Lie algebra has a unique invariant symmetric bilinear
form; possible cubic color tensors first enter the finite dimension-six block. Ward identities, rotation-defect
estimates, reflection-positive recombination, and Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction give covariance,
the unique vacuum, the gap, and noncollapse.

the displayed CG,h (1 + u−h ) hierarchy. A finite atlas covers the one-pivot compact fiber, so the score
constants are uniform in U , exterior data, volume, and preceding weak depth. Integrating the first score
along a geodesic of length at most diam G proves the oscillation bound. Marking one fixed factor uses
the corresponding marked rows.
   For a finite family of active straight macro-paths, keep every fine link on those active paths in its
original link coordinate. An active path carries one nontrivial retained Peter–Weyl coefficient, or one
bounded scalar probe whose first derivative at the origin is centered. Choose live pivots P = {p1 , . . . , pN }
among the original links of the active paths, with mutually disjoint buffered neighborhoods separated
by distance R and separated from all path endpoints. Condition on every nonpivot fine link, every link
outside the active paths, and all exterior/source data; denote this collection by η. Do not condition on a
retained path product carrying an active coefficient or probe.
   Assign every physical factor by its incidence in the original fine-link support: factors meeting no live
pivot enter H0 , complete owned factors meeting exactly pi enter the ith one-pivot weight, and connected
factors meeting at least two live pivots enter the multipivot remainder. The active retained carriers are
distinguished insertions and are never absorbed into a one-pivot density or counted as physical activities.

6.4    Finite-volume Perron input
Proposition 6.13 (Finite-volume Perron input from two-scale landing). For every finite spatial volume,
the one-step matching transfer kernel relative to product Haar is continuous, symmetric, and strictly
positive. If MΛ is the finite number of one-link updates in a sweep, then
                                                          −1
                                          KL (x, y) ≥ ϵM
                                                       ⋆ ZΛ,L > 0.
                                                        Λ



The compact transfer operator has a simple maximal eigenvalue and a unique strictly positive Perron
eigenfunction. No volume-uniform lower bound for the complete kernel is asserted.
Proof. Apply Theorem 6.10 with one live pivot at a time. Corollary 6.11 gives the finite-volume product
lower bound. The aligned half-step is SL∗ SL , so the transfer is positive and self-adjoint. Jentzsch–Perron
applies in finite volume.

6.5    Exact Haar–optical matching law
The matching macroblock used after the compact first crossing is the exact pushforward by oriented
length-L path products. It is useful to distinguish the coordinates that define the map from the coordinates
used to estimate a particular retained coefficient.
   Fix one proof color. Its straight macro-paths are pairwise edge-disjoint and have mutually disjoint
buffered interiors. For one path γ = (e1 , . . . , eL ) define
                                            Pγ (U ) = Ue1 · · · UeL .
The retained macro-link is Wγ = Pγ (U ). For paths not carrying an active coefficient one may use the
standard coordinates
                            Wγ = Pγ (U ),      Zγ,k = Uek , 2 ≤ k ≤ L,
with
                                         Ue1 = Wγ (Zγ,2 · · · Zγ,L )−1 .
The full map BL is the finite composition of the colorwise pushforwards, with the reflection plane on
macro-cell boundaries.

                                L

Consequently the simultaneous path-product map has unit Haar Jacobian, is gauge covariant at path
endpoints, and intertwines aligned reflection.
Proof. For fixed details, Ue1 7→ Wγ is right multiplication by a fixed group element. Haar invariance
proves the identity. Edge-disjointness tensorizes it, gauge transformations telescope, and reflection reverses
and inverts the product.

6.5.1 Compact collect with optical field live
The matching theorem is now proved on one exact joint law, before the normal/optical variables are
marginalized. This is the decisive ordering. The compact retained variables are reduced conditionally by
Haar–pivot integration; the resulting activities remain functions of the complete optical field; and only
then is the connected logarithm taken by the marked Gaussian forest theorem. Thus no retained density,
latent mixture, or residual-only gas is inserted between the physical law and the connected source kernel.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.

expectations or empty-support scalars and is assigned by the exact owner map to the normalized one-core
references or the pre-existing regular/Gaussian inventory.
   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial
internal flux, has a deterministic visited-set exploration. Order incident half-edges before marking an
unoriented edge inspected. Discovery edges form a rooted spanning tree; each merger, reconnection, shared
tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.

is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

11     Completion for arbitrary fixed compact simple gauge groups
Theorem 11.1 (Completion of the fixed-group construction). For every fixed compact connected simple
G and faithful unitary representation ρ, the group register CG is finite and all hypotheses consumed by
Sections 2–10 are satisfied. Consequently Theorem 1.1 holds.
Proof. Compactness and the analytic bi-invariant geometry give the Karcher, logarithm, coarea, and
faithful-action constants of Section 2. The complete folded block symbol is spacetime-only and tensors
with Ig , so the strict right-inverse and optical coercivity constants are unchanged. The chart complement
is charged by the faithful Wilson action and the irregular activity is exponentially small. The permanent
weak map, centered graph, and BPHZL packet use the same finite-dimensional Lie-algebra tensor calculus,
with the universal color factor CA (G).
   The Peter–Weyl spectral sum converges at the fixed order sG , and the higher hybrid-polydisc argument
supplies the one-pivot nuclear and multipivot Fourier–Wiener rows. The ordinary-periodic toron, seam,
reflection, and wrapping templates are admitted by Theorem D.3; no twisted sector or finite-volume bundle
sum is used. The invariant-jet theorem supplies the complete low-dimensional mixing and dimension-six
regulator spaces. The joint Haar–optical forest, source transport, Ward hierarchy, OS reconstruction,
and noncollapse theorem then apply with constants depending on G but uniform in cutoff, volume, and
directed depth. Appendix F, specifically Table 3, records every independent entry of CG , the first proof
call at which its G-dependence enters, and the subsequent consumers. Thus no additional estimate
uniform in G is hidden in this completion step: after those finite calls, each remaining mechanism is
color-free, tensors with Ig , or takes a finite maximum in a registered finite-dimensional space.
Corollary 11.2 (The SU(N ) family). For every fixed integer N ≥ 2, the theorem holds for G = SU(N )
in the defining representation, and the scale-two map is
                                               11N log 2
                             u(2L) = u(L) +              u(L)2 + ON (u(L)3 ).
                                                 24π 2
No estimate uniform as N → ∞ is asserted.
Remark 11.3 (Logical scope). The construction is a fixed-group theorem. The directed subsequence,
curvature-jet observable scope, and absence of a large-rank uniformity claim are part of the statement,
not omitted conclusions.

Lemma A.3 (Exact even-contact division of complete packets). For every complete packet class λ,
the one-open-leg coefficient vanishes by global color invariance. The renormalized two-open-leg packet is
reflection even, vanishes at p = 0, and admits the exact second-order division
                                                      X
                                    Tλ (p) − Tλ (0) =    pbα pbβ Sλ,αβ (p).                        (188)
                                                       α,β

For every 0 < a′ < a0 , the rooted norm of Sλ is bounded by the second support moment of the same
complete packet at exponent a0 .
   If the complete packet is represented at weak scale i, the two displayed difference factors carry the
canonical relative factor
                                             (r/ℓi )2 = 2−2i                                       (189)
with respect to the fixed physical source scale r. This factor belongs to the whole packet. It is not assigned
to a chosen branch or attachment cut.
Proof. The selector is inserted only after the exact normalized packet is formed and is scalar under color,
translation and aligned reflection. Hence every selected sum is again a complete packet. Its one-open-leg
coefficient is an invariant adjoint vector and therefore vanishes. Global contact subtraction is allocated
after the disjoint packet decomposition, so each selected renormalized coefficient vanishes at p = 0.
Reflection gives Tλ (−p) = Tλ (p) and therefore removes the linear Taylor term. The integral Taylor
formula, or equivalently finite Laurent telescoping in the variables eipα , gives (188). Two momentum
derivatives insert two support displacements, absorbed by the unused exponent a0 − a′ .
   The divided packet has no reflection-even scalar or rank-two local component of engineering dimension
four or five. Lemmas 5.22 and 5.23 therefore place its local projection in the stable degree-six block; this
observation will be used only for stable membership, not to estimate the nonlocal packet.
   The scale factor in (189) is instead purely geometric. In the tangent-normalized profile coordinates, one
lattice difference at representation scale ℓi = 2i r is (r/ℓi ) times the corresponding unit-scale difference.
The two explicit factors in (188) therefore contribute exactly (r/ℓi )2 = 2−2i . The two support moments
of Sλ are absorbed by the unused rooted exponent. This argument applies to the whole packet, local and
nonlocal together. Since the division identity holds for the entire C 2 family, zero, one or two g derivatives
do not remove the two explicit differences.

Lemma A.4 (g-marked one-scale admission). There is g0 > 0 such that, for real 0 ≤ g ≤ g0 , the complete
normalized interaction and all declared source/defect marks are twice continuously differentiable in the
permanent regulator space. An undistinguished non-Gaussian child has parent-normalized row

                                                 η0 (g) ≤ Cg,

while a child carrying one or two distinguished g derivatives has row

                                              η1 (g) + η2 (g) ≤ C.

The exactly recombined large-field/irregular row and its first two g derivatives extend continuously by zero
                                             2
at g = 0 and are bounded by Cm g −pm e−c/g for m ≤ 2. No claim that an attached odd child is O(g 2 ) is
made.
Proof. In the scale-normalized Gaussian coordinate, the cubic Yang–Mills species starts at order g, the
quartic and other non-Gaussian even species start at order g 2 , and the common species tube controls
all field and source marks. Thus an unmarked species row is Cg, while one or two explicit g derivatives
remove at most the corresponding powers and give a finite row. The regulator allocations are additive
under multiplication, and the Gram and Pruefer estimates in the summed replica–BKAR theorem are
insensitive to the parity of an attached tensor. The ordinary parent-normalized child recursion therefore
closes for Cg0 below its printed threshold, with two fixed derivative marks handled by Leibniz. The
C 3 -flat irregular estimate in u = g 2 gives the displayed first and second g-derivative rows after the chain
rule. In particular the model child gA3 differentiated once by a covariance edge is correctly admitted as
an O(g) child, and one g derivative of that child is O(1).

E     Invariant tensor spaces through engineering dimension six
The low-dimensional color input can be stated without choosing a basis. The degree-two invariant
polynomial is unique for every simple g. A primitive degree-three invariant occurs only for Ar , r ≥ 2.
Hence the reflection-even dimension-four scalar block is one-dimensional for every G, while the dimension-
six block may contain the additional cubic curvature contraction in type A. The antisymmetric structure


                                                      111
tensor is always present through the bracket but contributes only inside the already retained covariant
derivative and commutator jets.
   The manuscript uses the complete finite quotient generated by curvature, covariant derivatives, metric
and epsilon contractions, invariant color tensors, total-difference classes, and equation-of-motion contacts
through the declared engineering cutoff. No argument relies on a hand-picked SU(2) basis once this
quotient is used.

F      Theorem-level specialization and dependency map
The purpose of this appendix is provenance rather than a new estimate. It identifies every independent
fixed-group input in the register CG , the first proof call at which that dependence enters, and the later
statements that consume it. In particular, the completion proof in Theorem 11.1 does not rely on an
unprinted constant or on a rank-one identity.

   The table also separates the common mechanisms into four logical classes. Replica–BKAR, Kotecký–
Preiss, history compatibility, support reporting, least-label source forests, OS reconstruction, and spectral-
gap promotion are color-free. The full-alias symbol, normal right inverse, optical split, and spacetime
BPHZL degrees tensor with Ig . Karcher, action-charge, Peter–Weyl, and ordinary-periodic template
estimates enter only through the finite constants displayed above. Invariant jets and dimension-six color
tensors are enlarged finite spaces rather than rank-one identities.
   The rank-one paper [14] is obtained by taking G = SU(2), sG = 1, and a trivial cubic invariant space.
This map is comparative; the present proof does not invoke the rank-one theorem.

G      Representative fixed-group certifications
This appendix instantiates the finite ledgers for three non-rank-one groups. For a faithful representation
ρ, let Iρ > 0 be its Dynkin index in the declared invariant metric,
                                     − Tr dρ(X)dρ(Y ) = Iρ ⟨X, Y ⟩.
                                                        

The representation-normalized Wilson function has the expansion
                                                     cρ Iρ
                                      wG,ρ (eX ) =         ∥X∥2 + O(∥X∥4 ).
                                                     2dρ
The declared background-field convention fixes the positive scalar cρ ; any equivalent choice is related by
a finite linear change of the bare coupling.


                                                        113
SU(4).    Use the defining faithful representation on C4 :

                                                           1
                                                               
                                      wG,ρ (U ) = cρ 1 − Re Tr U .
                                                           4

Then dG = 15, CA (G) = 4, sG = 4, and 2sG = 8 > 15/2. The degree-three invariant is present and is
included in the dimension-six jet block. The scale-two coefficient is 11 log 2/(6π 2 ). The charge vanishes
precisely at I4 and is positive away from it, so Theorem 3.4 applies with the representation-normalized
deficit rather than a rank-one raw trace.

Sp(2) (USp(4)).        Use the standard faithful four-dimensional complex representation:

                                                          1
                                                                   
                                      wG,ρ (U ) = cρ 1 − Re Tr U .
                                                          4

Here dG = 10, CA (G) = 3, sG = 3, and 2sG = 6 > 5. There is no primitive cubic invariant, and the
coefficient is 11 log 2/(8π 2 ). The same faithful-action and differentiated charged-core ledger applies.

G2 . Use the faithful seven-dimensional real fundamental representation, viewed unitarily after complexi-
fication:
                                                     1
                                                                 
                                  wG,ρ (U ) = cρ 1 − Re Tr ρ(U ) .
                                                     7
Then dG = 14, CA (G) = 4, sG = 4, and 2sG = 8 > 7. There is no primitive cubic invariant and the
coefficient is 11 log 2/(6π 2 ). Faithfulness again makes the identity the unique zero of the charge.
   For all three examples, the compact ordinary-periodic toron set TG ⊂ G4 is covered by Lemma D.2;
Theorem D.3 then supplies the same color-free full-alias and optical constants. The spectral sum in
Appendix C converges at the displayed orders, while all nonlinear constants remain finite and group
dependent. These are concrete admissions, not hypotheses of the main theorem.

   The one-pivot oscillation is precisely the complete one-pivot ledger proved above; normalization changes
only an U -independent scalar. For the multipivot row, every activity is reported in its original connected
fine-link support. Split it by the three species in Proposition 6.8. A reference factor meeting separated
pivots has diam A ≥ cp R(|IP (A)| − 1); a regular or irregular connected factor has |A| ≥ cp R(|IP (A)| − 1).
Reserve respectively mref − a′ref , areg − a′reg , and airr − a′irr in the three input rows. After multiplying
by the pivot charge eλ|IP (A)| , the reserved exponent absorbs that charge for sufficiently large finite R
and yields exactly the three terms of ∆R (u). Thus no diameter estimate is used to pay a spanning-tree
weight. Coordinate substitutions on inactive paths are independent of all live pivots and cannot create
additional pivot incidence. Physical-source marks of order at most two change only Cλ ; the independent
pivot derivatives through order 2sG are already included in the three norms in (HT5).
   Finally, on an active path no anchor is reconstructed: all path links remain original variables. Splitting
the ordered path product immediately gives (49). Haar invariance therefore annihilates the Haar part of
every nontrivial carrier at an uncovered pivot under the same integral in which the product reference was
obtained.

6.5.1 Compact collect with optical field live
The matching theorem is now proved on one exact joint law, before the normal/optical variables are
marginalized. This is the decisive ordering. The compact retained variables are reduced conditionally by
Haar–pivot integration; the resulting activities remain functions of the complete optical field; and only
then is the connected logarithm taken by the marked Gaussian forest theorem. Thus no retained density,
latent mixture, or residual-only gas is inserted between the physical law and the connected source kernel.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.

expectations or empty-support scalars and is assigned by the exact owner map to the normalized one-core
references or the pre-existing regular/Gaussian inventory.
   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial
internal flux, has a deterministic visited-set exploration. Order incident half-edges before marking an
unoriented edge inspected. Discovery edges form a rooted spanning tree; each merger, reconnection, shared
tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.25 (Complete compact-flux classification and canonical exploration). Fix ζ and take the
Peter–Weyl decomposition of the complete compact incidence network generated by the exact pushforward
under BL . Integrate all compact variables coefficientwise. A connected history is compact-vacuum only
when every compact cut separating distinct mixed optical/source vertices carries the trivial representation.
After removal of already reported physical cross-core connectors, such a history factorizes into one-core
expectations or empty-support scalars and is assigned by the exact owner map to the normalized one-core
references or the pre-existing regular/Gaussian inventory.
   Every remaining history, including a multi-leg singlet with trivial visible coarse label but nontrivial
internal flux, has a deterministic visited-set exploration. Order incident half-edges before marking an
unoriented edge inspected. Discovery edges form a rooted spanning tree; each merger, reconnection, shared
tail, cycle, seam, reflection, or wrapping edge is a uniquely owned closure edge. The record reconstructs
the occupied geometric network without duplicating shared continuations.

Proof. Vacuum factorization follows by deleting the reported physical connectors and applying Fubini
across every trivial compact cut. Otherwise the least mixed cut, least nontrivial representation label, and
least oriented half-edge choose the root and first edge. Deterministic depth-first exploration then classifies
every occupied unoriented edge exactly once as a discovery or closure edge. A composite singlet is retained
whenever any internal separating cut is nontrivial, independently of the visible output label.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

Lemma 6.37 (Carrier–activity hypergraph coverage and no-reuse allocation). For a connected family
(g, F) form the finite incidence hypergraph Hg,F whose ordinary edges are the physical carrier segments and
whose hyperedge A is incident to the selected pivots IP (A). Root the carrier skeleton by the deterministic
order of Lemma 6.34. Then:
    (i) cutting every carrier at U (F) ∪ Rg (F) leaves an acyclic carrier graph;
   (ii) the depth-first first-incidence rule assigns every activity hyperedge A exactly once, at the least
        incident pivot first reached from the root; its remaining n(A) − 1 incidences are recorded only as
        possible side branches;
  (iii) the three payments are disjoint: the product Fourier–Wiener norm pays the tensor-product nuclear
        cost on U (F), the scalar coverage reserve pays the lost clean-pivot contractions, and the promoted
        magnitude wA,k(A) is inserted exactly once in the rooted spatial recursion.
Consequently no same-edge or cross-edge activity, shared carrier tail, closure edge, or cycle-breaking pivot
is charged twice in (90) or in the recursion (94).
Proof. By definition, every carrier cycle meeting an activity is cut at all of that activity’s incident pivots,
and every remaining activity-free carrier cycle is cut at its least closure pivot in Rg (F). Hence a cycle in
the residual carrier graph would avoid both sets, contradicting (87); this proves (i). On the resulting
rooted forest, deterministic depth-first exploration gives a total order on first visits to pivots. Assign a
hyperedge at the first visited member of its incidence set. This assignment is unique, while every other
incidence can only attach a branch to an already assigned hyperedge, proving (ii). The product-group
convolution of Lemma 6.35 contains the complete activity factor and all covered one-pivot densities before
any scalar split. Lemma 6.31 then separates its nuclear loss from the unused scalar incidence reserve.
The first-incidence exploration retains one and only one copy of the promoted activity magnitude. These
operations act on distinct factors of the majorant, proving (iii) and the final claim.

trivialization. The 2sG differentiated bad-core row of Theorem 3.20 is therefore uniform on the same
cover. Consequently the complete one-pivot score and Haar minorization retain their printed constants
after taking the finite template maximum. On intersections use the fixed least-label owner, so no factor is
duplicated. A wrapping certificate records only the four lattice directions, the fixed block range, a finite
seam crossing pattern, and an aligned reflection type; there are finitely many such local templates at one
normalized step. Their iteration is already controlled by the permanent wrapping ideal rather than by a
sum over topological sectors. Taking the finite maximum proves the stated admission and leaves the joint
Haar–optical boundary-to-center mechanism unchanged.

E     Invariant tensor spaces through engineering dimension six
The low-dimensional color input can be stated without choosing a basis. The degree-two invariant
polynomial is unique for every simple g. A primitive degree-three invariant occurs only for Ar , r ≥ 2.
Hence the reflection-even dimension-four scalar block is one-dimensional for every G, while the dimension-
six block may contain the additional cubic curvature contraction in type A. The antisymmetric structure


                                                      111
tensor is always present through the bracket but contributes only inside the already retained covariant
derivative and commutator jets.
   The manuscript uses the complete finite quotient generated by curvature, covariant derivatives, metric
and epsilon contractions, invariant color tensors, total-difference classes, and equation-of-motion contacts
through the declared engineering cutoff. No argument relies on a hand-picked SU(2) basis once this
quotient is used.

F      Theorem-level specialization and dependency map

fixed-group input in the register CG , the first proof call at which that dependence enters, and the later
statements that consume it. In particular, the completion proof in Theorem 11.1 does not rely on an
unprinted constant or on a rank-one identity.

Theorem 6.39 (Exact incidence-split product-group nuclear compact collect). Choose R and a finite
pivot count N from the unmarked conditions (84), (95), and (96), with N ≥ 3. These choices are made
once and are independent of source order. Then, for every fixed Q < ∞, after exact compact integration
the complete nonvacuum compact coefficients satisfy (99), uniformly through three passive optical marks
and Q physical-source marks. The constants have the Cauchy growth of one common positive source
radius.
Proof. Expand the exact single-denominator amplitude once by Lemma 6.34 and split every activity
by (71). For each family, absorb all covered-pivot densities and all same-edge or cross-edge activity
factors into the one product-group convolution operator of Lemma 6.35. Its Fourier–Wiener norm pays
the actual tensor-product nuclear cost. The scalar incidence reserve pays that cost and every lost Haar
contraction, while the promoted activity magnitude remains once for the canonical rooted exploration.
Clean activity-free physical cycles are closed at the deterministic pivots in Rg (F). The strict unmarked
recursion fixes R and N once. At every finite marked order the same-order coefficient is still qsp < 1
and all new terms are lower-triangular forcing, so source order changes constants but not the chosen
geometry. The marked triangular extension sums all carrier branches, physical cycles, shared tails, seams,
reflections, wrapping edges, and activity hyperedges. The resulting majorant proves absolute convergence
of the family expansion and permits the cutoff and finite-subfamily limits. The final spatial allocation
gives (99).

The matching theorem is now proved on one exact joint law, before the normal/optical variables are
marginalized. This is the decisive ordering. The compact retained variables are reduced conditionally by
Haar–pivot integration; the resulting activities remain functions of the complete optical field; and only
then is the connected logarithm taken by the marked Gaussian forest theorem. Thus no retained density,
latent mixture, or residual-only gas is inserted between the physical law and the connected source kernel.

Lemma 7.6 (Vacuum factorization after the complete owner map). Fix the optical variables and expand
one compact coefficient in Peter–Weyl sectors. Suppose every compact cut separating two declared root
buffers carries the trivial representation. Remove only the cross-core objects already registered in the
four disjoint inventories of Corollary 6.40. If no registered connector remains between the roots, the
residual coefficient factorizes into one-core expectations and empty-support scalars. Its contribution to the
normalized connected two-root logarithm is zero.
Proof. Triviality on every separating compact cut permits repeated Haar–Fubini separation. The exact

other cross-core occurrence to exactly one of AJG , AJreg , AJirr , or AJH . After those registered objects are
removed, the residual history has no object joining distinct one-core components. It therefore factorizes.
Empty-support scalars are removed by the normalization, and products of separate one-root expectations
are removed by the connected logarithm.
Theorem 7.7 (Exact acoustic exclusion-or-capture). Consider any connected zero-, one-, or two-source
coefficient joining two bounded matching-scale root buffers in the exact joint logarithm. At least one object
on the unique root-to-root forest path belongs to one of the following classes:
   (i) a nonvacuum compact activity controlled by Theorem 6.39 and the spatial row (99);
  (ii) an optical covariance bond or an optical Gaussian cross-core activity in AJG ;
 (iii) a registered reference, regular, irregular, seam, reflection, wrapping, normalization, determinant, or
       source connector with its original support payment.
There is no fourth class consisting of a massless retained acoustic reference edge.
Proof. Assume that a connected coefficient contains no object of types (i)–(iii). Absence of (i) makes
every separating compact cut vacuum. Absence of (iii) leaves no registered physical connector after the
complete owner map. Lemma 7.6 then reduces the compact contribution to disconnected one-core factors
and scalars. Absence of (ii) also prevents the still-live optical field from joining the roots. The coefficient
is therefore disconnected, a contradiction. The only possible remaining concern would be an undeclared
massless retained covariance, which is excluded by Lemma 7.5.

Lemma 7.5 (No massless retained reference at matching). In the exact post-compact joint partition of

Proof. The exact compact collect of Theorem 6.39 and the post-compact identity of Corollary 6.40 restore

Lemma 7.6 (Vacuum factorization after the complete owner map). Fix the optical variables and expand
one compact coefficient in Peter–Weyl sectors. Suppose every compact cut separating two declared root
buffers carries the trivial representation. Remove only the cross-core objects already registered in the
four disjoint inventories of Corollary 6.40. If no registered connector remains between the roots, the
residual coefficient factorizes into one-core expectations and empty-support scalars. Its contribution to the
normalized connected two-root logarithm is zero.
Proof. Triviality on every separating compact cut permits repeated Haar–Fubini separation. The exact
incidence-split collect retains every internally nontrivial singlet in AJH , while the owner map assigns every
other cross-core occurrence to exactly one of AJG , AJreg , AJirr , or AJH . After those registered objects are
removed, the residual history has no object joining distinct one-core components. It therefore factorizes.
Empty-support scalars are removed by the normalization, and products of separate one-root expectations
are removed by the connected logarithm.
Theorem 7.7 (Exact acoustic exclusion-or-capture). Consider any connected zero-, one-, or two-source
coefficient joining two bounded matching-scale root buffers in the exact joint logarithm. At least one object
on the unique root-to-root forest path belongs to one of the following classes:
   (i) a nonvacuum compact activity controlled by Theorem 6.39 and the spatial row (99);
  (ii) an optical covariance bond or an optical Gaussian cross-core activity in AJG ;
 (iii) a registered reference, regular, irregular, seam, reflection, wrapping, normalization, determinant, or
       source connector with its original support payment.
There is no fourth class consisting of a massless retained acoustic reference edge.
Proof. Assume that a connected coefficient contains no object of types (i)–(iii). Absence of (i) makes
every separating compact cut vacuum. Absence of (iii) leaves no registered physical connector after the
complete owner map. Lemma 7.6 then reduces the compact contribution to disconnected one-core factors
and scalars. Absence of (ii) also prevents the still-live optical field from joining the roots. The coefficient
is therefore disconnected, a contradiction. The only possible remaining concern would be an undeclared
massless retained covariance, which is excluded by Lemma 7.5.

Proof. The vertex inventory is already exhaustive by Lemma 6.7, Proposition 6.8, and Corollary 6.40.

Lemma 7.5 (No massless retained reference at matching). In the exact post-compact joint partition of
Corollary 6.40, the retained compact field has product normalized Haar reference and has already been
integrated coefficientwise before the optical connected logarithm is taken. The massless tangent Feynman
Gaussian used in the weak normal-chart construction is not a live matching reference. The only Gaussian
reference left live is the normalized optical one-core product, and every cross-core optical term is contained
in the explicit inventory AJG .
Proof. The exact compact collect of Theorem 6.39 and the post-compact identity of Corollary 6.40 restore
product Haar on the retained compact variables and place every nonempty retained dependence into the
compact, Gaussian, regular, or irregular activity inventories. The weak tangent Gaussian contributes
no undeclared covariance edge to this matching logarithm. By contrast, the optical one-core references
remain live, while their off-diagonal quadratic blocks and other cross-core terms occur explicitly in AJG
and retain the spatial payment used in Theorem 6.43.
Lemma 7.6 (Vacuum factorization after the complete owner map). Fix the optical variables and expand
one compact coefficient in Peter–Weyl sectors. Suppose every compact cut separating two declared root
buffers carries the trivial representation. Remove only the cross-core objects already registered in the
four disjoint inventories of Corollary 6.40. If no registered connector remains between the roots, the
residual coefficient factorizes into one-core expectations and empty-support scalars. Its contribution to the
normalized connected two-root logarithm is zero.
Proof. Triviality on every separating compact cut permits repeated Haar–Fubini separation. The exact
incidence-split collect retains every internally nontrivial singlet in AJH , while the owner map assigns every
other cross-core occurrence to exactly one of AJG , AJreg , AJirr , or AJH . After those registered objects are
removed, the residual history has no object joining distinct one-core components. It therefore factorizes.
Empty-support scalars are removed by the normalization, and products of separate one-root expectations
are removed by the connected logarithm.
Theorem 7.7 (Exact acoustic exclusion-or-capture). Consider any connected zero-, one-, or two-source
coefficient joining two bounded matching-scale root buffers in the exact joint logarithm. At least one object
on the unique root-to-root forest path belongs to one of the following classes:
   (i) a nonvacuum compact activity controlled by Theorem 6.39 and the spatial row (99);
  (ii) an optical covariance bond or an optical Gaussian cross-core activity in AJG ;
 (iii) a registered reference, regular, irregular, seam, reflection, wrapping, normalization, determinant, or
       source connector with its original support payment.
There is no fourth class consisting of a massless retained acoustic reference edge.
Proof. Assume that a connected coefficient contains no object of types (i)–(iii). Absence of (i) makes
every separating compact cut vacuum. Absence of (iii) leaves no registered physical connector after the
complete owner map. Lemma 7.6 then reduces the compact contribution to disconnected one-core factors
and scalars. Absence of (ii) also prevents the still-live optical field from joining the roots. The coefficient
is therefore disconnected, a contradiction. The only possible remaining concern would be an undeclared
massless retained covariance, which is excluded by Lemma 7.5.

Corollary 7.8 (No additional acoustic path class). The exact vertex inventory used in Theorem 6.43 ad-
mits no fourth root-to-root path class consisting of a massless retained acoustic reference edge. Consequently
the boundary-to-center estimates (104) and (107) require no additional terminal Witten, acoustic-channel,
or retained-Gaussian gap hypothesis.
Proof. The vertex inventory is already exhaustive by Lemma 6.7, Proposition 6.8, and Corollary 6.40.
Apply Theorem 7.7 to exclude the only remaining acoustic fourth-class concern.
